touches.text: WHY: So everything the system learns is one connected body the librarian can see whole, and patterns can be exported from all of it. And so no device invents its own way of storing things: there are two ways, and every device uses them.

The librarian owns every tree and delegates ownership of some to the devices that learn: CodeMother, chart, any learning block holds its own trees by the librarian's delegation (Law 6: delegation through the owner's gate). Why: two holders with different weights over the same nodes have different perspectives and can debate points, and the librarian, asked anything, can look at the query from both. (Akien 2026-11-05)

Delegation nests down the rungs: the librarian delegates a set of trees to a device, the device to its machines, a machine to its tools if one is ever that complex. Each stays co-owned by the one above. CodeMother's learning goes in its own tables, and she owns the learning blocks of her machines and tools. (Akien 2026-11-05)

Not every node gets an embedding. Embedding every single thing would make an impossible mound of data, and that is not how Akien works, and this is meant to work the way he does. What gets embedded is the pattern: the answers to a few key questions that cross domains. "How might that work" is chief among them: "it's applicable in almost all domains, and captures the pattern, not the domain specific answer." A node without an embedding is found by its key (eg an exact request). (Akien 2026-11-05, open-029c5ae100a9) Which questions those are: 4.3.1.11. (Q#65, Akien 2026-11-05)

Cross-domain questions: a special kind of question, inherently cross domain (or cognition questions), not domain specific. "How might that work?" is Akien's number one. They are not design questions: a design question is a spec choice waiting on Akien (cairn question, CairnCommons/questions/). (Akien 2026-11-05)

A question is a node in the one list (4.3.1.8.1). Questions can belong to devices, and two devices can have the same question: both hold the same node. A device that owns a question is a delegate, because all knowledge belongs ultimately to the librarian (4.3.1.6). Owning a question = holding a tree for it, with that device's own weights.

The answers to cross-domain questions are what get embedded (4.3.1.8.1.1): an answer from any domain lands in that question's tree as a pattern, so a later search under the same question finds patterns from other domains ("which often initiates a cross domain search", Akien 2026-07-14).

The corpus is a git JSON file beside the librarian's code (shareable spec, 4.3.4); the question trees are derived from it. Every entry carries its origin: verbatim (Akien's words, with date and source) or proposed (by CC, by Gemini, ...). All questions are included; the origin keeps his words apart. (Akien 2026-11-05: "we can include all the questions. i expect i have a couple of hundred in my own head.")

Questions that fire in sequence are linked "followed by" in the shared link list (4.3.1.8.4), so a walk can run a sequence. Two known: mechanism, need, fit, get inside, experiment (Novelty.txt 2026-07-14); best pattern, gaps, trim to fit, how might that work (cortical columns, 2026-07-02).

Harvest: a deterministic pass over Akien's logs and notes proposes question-shaped lines in his words; he confirms each before it is marked verbatim. New ones are added through a librarian command as he says them.

NOT HOW IT IS NOW (measured 2026-11-05): the corpus lives in CodeMother (cairn/devices/codemother/cognition_questions.json, embedded by seed_trees.py) with 13 of UU's 18 verbatim questions (Q-cog-014..018 lost in the move), Akien's 3 from Novelty.txt, and 11 Gemini-worded questions labelled "Akien verbatim".
Shareable provenance (charters, tickets, validations) is git JSON beside the code, never a row.
Owns the graph trees: the one list of nodes, and each depositor's index over them (4.3.1.2).
TOOLS: trees (its own, published as a client tool); base, question, bus_client, system_word, gate; machine learning_block; db client
